goal_checks.notes: Exactly the four route files architecture.blueprint.json commands[] names exist — POST /api/v1/workspaces, POST /api/v1/highlights/:id/mini-conclusion, POST /api/v1/workspaces/:id/results, GET /api/v1/runs/:id/stream — and no fifth. commands.test.ts pins the count and the on-disk set; verify:arch I15 fails on any undeclared route; the production build emits the four as dynamic routes.

Each handler binds, calls one service (createWorkspace / requestMiniConclusion / requestResult / subscribeRun) and maps a typed error through http.ts. No route contains a table read, an rpc call or the domain rule: commands.test.ts scans for `.from(`, `.rpc(`, `can_lead_session`, `pipeline_runs`, `profile_identities`; the group-leader branch lives in requestResult and is unit-tested there.

src/server now has the spec §4.2 members, each with a real member and no empty placeholder: db/ (client, errors, rpc), pipeline/ (service, stages/registry.ts), memory/ (service), llm/ (service). The folders mirror the future Go packages; renames in that port stay moves, not rewrites.

requestContext validates the bearer, builds a request-scoped client from the one shared seam (createUserClient) and resolves the caller's profile through their own RLS-readable identity row. There is no secret or service-role key anywhere: createUserClient uses only the publishable key, and both the i21 lint rule and commands.test.ts's `supabase` scan guard against a second import site. client.test.ts pins the 401 paths.

requestResult checks can_lead_session(target_session) for a group scope and raises ForbiddenError before any insert; the route maps it to 403. service.test.ts proves the refusal writes nothing and that a leader's group run stores owner_profile_id null; route-handlers.test.ts proves the 403. RLS continues to enforce the same at the row (D-03); the live-RLS confirmation is a follow-up.

cross_check_against_plan.result: matches — backend; the five mini-goals map to g1-g5; it blocks 018 and does not open it.

matches — the API surface is exactly the four endpoints; the server folders mirror §4.2; no service-role key (RULE-01); handlers bind/call/map (RULE-22); llm/ is the only key-resolving module (RULE-24); no endpoint was added that RLS could serve (RULE-23).
matches — pipeline_runs(mode, owner_profile_id, status) and can_lead_session(target_session) are used as defined; sessions.default_mode supplies the fallback mode; no schema change.
matches — the four commands and their route paths are implemented verbatim; no fifth.

issues_found: The 403 path is proven at the handler/service boundary with the fake client; confirming it against the live RLS stack (task 002's suite) is a follow-up, like the other stack-dependent gates.
D-12 still blocks 018, so src/server/llm/service.ts is the interface only and throws LlmUnavailableError; no provider is configured and none is named (RULE-24 respected).

The result route's request body is `{ scope, mode? }`: spec §4.3 names only `scope`, so an omitted mode falls back to the session's default_mode column rather than inventing one. Recorded as a decision.

The mini-conclusion service reports `queued` and does not persist a job: no queue table exists, and 019 owns the debounce/cache/generation. The endpoint is real (it performs an RLS-scoped read) but its enqueue is 019's.
create-workspace's service lives in src/server/db/rpc.ts because §4.2 lists no workspace package; flagged so the Go port can move it deliberately.
